title: Why does cooling improve CCD sensitivity?

segments.text: Why does cooling improve CCD sensitivity?
Photons generate electrons directly in the MOS capacitor, achieving up to 95 percent quantum efficiency.
Each well stores roughly 100000 electrons before it overflows.
Dark‑current processes in the depletion region, at the surface, and in the neutral bulk add unwanted charge, limiting how long you can integrate light.
Cooling the sensor slows these dark‑current mechanisms, reducing noise and allowing more useful photons to be collected.
Less noise means the stored charge reflects the scene more accurately, so cooling improves CCD sensitivity.
